title: A Ledger for the Verdict
premise: Retired detective Edmund Blackwood, who has quietly solved three deaths the police dismissed as accidents, is drawn into a fourth case when a missing woman's diary turns up in his failing bookshop—its entries continuing for months after her disappearance. As Edmund decodes a hidden ledger woven into the shop's own inventory, he uncovers an inheritance scheme entwined with his own buried past and the identity of the woman he failed to save years ago. The trail converges on the annual Verdict family anniversary dinner, where the killer intends to finalize the inheritance and erase the last witness. Edmund must expose the truth at the table itself, sacrificing his invisibility to finally claim the identity he has spent a decade hiding from.
about_author: Xanthe Thornbury is the pen name of a former estate archivist who spent fifteen years cataloguing the private papers of old moneyed families before turning to fiction. Her debut novels are known for their obsession with documents, dust, and the quiet violence of inheritance.

chapters.title: The Shop That Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund Blackwood tends his failing bookshop, cataloguing a deceased estate's donation when he notices a diary with no checkout record. The opening establishes his invisibility, his quiet pride in three unofficially solved deaths, and the shop as a character. Emotional beat: restless contentment about to crack.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. The diary belongs to Marion Verdict, reported missing eleven months ago; the final dated entries continue four months past her disappearance, in handwriting Edmund confirms is hers. He realizes either she lives or someone with access to her hand is writing. Emotional beat: the thrill of a case reawakening a dormant self.

chapters.title: What the Police Filed Away
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund visits his former protégé, DS Imogen Reyes, and reads the thin missing-persons file: Marion vanished before her family's anniversary dinner, leaving no note. The file's neatness bothers him—too tidy, curated. Emotional beat: professional unease sharpening into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Ledger Hidden in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Cross-referencing diary references to 'accounts' with the shop's donated stock, Edmund discovers the ledger: numbers encoded in book prices and shelf positions, tracking money moved through the Verdict family trust. Emotional beat: the hunter's joy, and dread—someone donated this collection deliberately, to him.

chapters.title: Marion, In Her Own Hand
chapters.summary: POV Edmund, with diary excerpts. The entries reveal Marion auditing the family trust, discovering siphoned funds, and fearing 'the one who signs.' She trusted only a bookshop owner she never names. Emotional beat: intimacy with a voice that may already be dead.

chapters.title: An Invitation to Dinner
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. An engraved invitation arrives: the Verdict family's annual anniversary dinner, addressed to Edmund by his real, abandoned name. Someone knows who he is. Emotional beat: terror—his decade of invisibility is over.

chapters.title: Three Accidents, Reconsidered
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund revisits his three quiet solutions and finds they share a thread: all three victims were trust auditors or witnesses connected to the Verdict estate. His past cases were never separate—they were the same killer clearing a path. Emotional beat: horror at the pattern he touched but never joined.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Daughter
chapters.summary: POV Imogen Reyes. Reyes, uneasy about Edmund's off-book interest, investigates Marion's employer and finds Marion was the illegitimate daughter of the trust's founder—the true heir the family denies. Emotional beat: Reyes's loyalty to procedure warring with loyalty to Edmund.

chapters.title: A Break-in, Neatly Done
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. The shop is searched overnight; nothing stolen except pages 40 through 55 of the diary. The intruder knew exactly which entries mattered. Edmund realizes the ledger's key was in those pages. Emotional beat: violation, and the cold comfort of being feared.

chapters.title: The One Who Signs
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Reconstructing the trust's signatures, Edmund narrows the suspects: the widowed matriarch, the charming son Alistair, and the family solicitor, Mr. Pell. Each has an alibi built on the same dinner guest list. Emotional beat: methodical calm masking rising dread.

chapters.title: Reyes Draws a Line
chapters.summary: POV Imogen Reyes. Reyes confronts Edmund: help her solve it properly or she'll arrest him for obstruction. She reveals a fourth 'accident'—a fall last spring—filed the week Marion disappeared. Emotional beat: fractured partnership becoming an uneasy alliance.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Guest List
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund attends the Verdict estate's open rehearsal under a false name and maps the house, the guests, the toasts. Alistair recognizes him—or pretends to. Emotional beat: the predator and prey roles blurring deliciously.

chapters.title: Pages 40 to 55
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund realizes the missing pages described the ledger's cipher key—and that the shop's own shelving order, unchanged since the donation, reproduces it. The donor wanted the ledger findable, but only by someone patient. Emotional beat: revelation as inheritance—the collection was left to him.

chapters.title: The Heir Who Wasn't Missing
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. The decoded ledger shows Marion alive and withdrawing funds under a new identity after her 'disappearance'—she staged it to flee. But the entries kept coming in her hand after she vanished for real. Someone found her. Emotional beat: hope curdling into grief.

chapters.title: What Edmund Buried
chapters.summary: POV Edmund, flashback-tinged. Edmund confronts why he retired: a case where his testimony destroyed an innocent woman, after which he erased his name. Marion's diary quotes a retired detective's published error—she was investigating him, too. Emotional beat: shame meeting purpose.

chapters.title: The Solicitor's Confession, Almost
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund corners Pell, who admits the trust is hollow and that 'the family' ordered the audits silenced—but Pell flees before naming who signs. That night Pell's office burns. Emotional beat: the cost of asking questions, paid in someone else's blood.

chapters.title: Reyes Finds the Body
chapters.summary: POV Imogen Reyes. Pell's death is ruled accidental; Reyes, now convinced, illegally shares the arson report with Edmund. A watch fragment in the ashes matches Alistair's engraved cufflink set. Emotional beat: Reyes crossing her own Rubicon.

chapters.title: The Cipher Completes
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. The final ledger entry, decoded, names the signatory and reveals Marion hid the trust's true deed inside a book donated to the shop—a first edition Edmund has sold and re-bought three times. Emotional beat: everything he needed was on his own shelves.

chapters.title: An Invitation Accepted
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund sends his RSVP. He prepares the shop as a dead-drop, leaves the decoded evidence with Reyes, and dresses for the dinner knowing he may not return. Emotional beat: a man choosing to be seen, whatever it costs.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Amid toasts, Edmund accuses Alistair before the family, presenting the ledger and Marion's final entries. Alistair confesses obliquely—Marion died fleeing him—and moves to silence Edmund, but Reyes arrives with the arson warrant. Emotional beat: climax; truth spoken aloud at last, at the table built on lies.

chapters.title: The Verdict of the Living
chapters.summary: POV Imogen Reyes. Alistair is arrested; the matriarch, complicit in silence, dissolves the trust, and Marion's heirship is acknowledged posthumously. Reyes and Edmund negotiate a fragile truce—his methods, her badge. Emotional beat: justice imperfect but real.

chapters.title: A Ledger Closed
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund reopens the shop with new signage bearing his true name, files Marion's diary beside his three old case notes, and writes the first entry in a ledger of his own. The fourth death is solved; the invisible man is visible. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace.
